objective: Extend the robot structural foundation with a bottom-up metallic fracture-mechanics and damage-tolerance concept article, a foundational-paper reconstruction, a current-research reconstruction, causal responsive visualizations, Korean-annotated KaTeX, public deployment and a replayable small-model record.

curriculum_decision.observed_gap: The structural article stopped at nominal stress, S-N screening and cumulative damage. The curriculum only mentioned cracks incidentally and did not teach flaw idealization, crack driving force, resistance, growth, residual strength, NDE capability or inspection decisions.
curriculum_decision.selected_layer: Metallic fracture mechanics and damage tolerance
curriculum_decision.why_now: It consumes the load path, stress spectrum, material and FEA states already established by structural mechanics and produces the initial conditions needed by inspection and lifecycle management.
curriculum_decision.deferred: Composite delamination, anisotropic laminate failure and barely visible impact damage require a separate next layer because metallic K-based transfer would create false competence.

private_transfer_problem.scenario: A 7075-T73 hollow robot shoulder shaft has a bearing fillet, lubrication hole, qualified NDE limit, a detected semi-elliptical indication, bending/torsion spectrum, emergency brake load, residual stress, temperature range and chloride exposure. Coupon toughness/growth data and component thickness do not match exactly; FEA and NASGRO-style results require interpretation.
premise_groups: modes, Griffith energy balance and G
K field, geometry factor and stress decomposition
plastic zone, constraint, thickness and toughness transfer
critical crack, residual strength and geometry transition
Delta K, R, threshold, full-range growth, sequence and environment
primary versus secondary stress and FAD
NDE POD, assumed flaw, inspection and proof test
private_transfer_problem.reader_gate: An article-only reader should be able to construct and criticize a flaw-to-inspection ledger for an unseen metallic robot component without treating a solver pass/fail as certification.

source_selection.source: A. A. Griffith, The Phenomena of Rupture and Flow in Solids, 1921
source_selection.selection_reason: It is the bottom-up origin of the energy-balance question and flaw-size scaling.
source_selection.durable_claim: Crack extension competes through released elastic energy and resistance; critical stress decreases with flaw size.
source_selection.boundary_preserved: The final Author's Note requires correction of the cracked-plate strain-energy calculation and numerical equations 6-13, and reconsideration of experimental verification. Molecular-orientation sections are historical speculation rather than current fracture mechanism.

source_selection.source: NASA-TM-103591, Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics Primer, 1992
source_selection.selection_reason: It bridges Griffith energy, Irwin K fields, plastic-zone screens, toughness, subcritical growth and fracture control without using a software black box.
source_selection.boundary_preserved: A primer and rules of thumb are not current product allowables or certification requirements.

source_selection.selection_reason: It provides a rigorous design-analysis-test-NDE-tracking process, assumed-flaw linkage, spectrum requirements and 90/95 NDE relationship.
source_selection.boundary_preserved: It governs applicable human-rated spaceflight hardware and is used here as a process example, not automatically imposed on robots.

source_selection.source: NASA/CR-20250011200, Fitness-For-Service Assessments of Crack-Like Flaws Using NASGRO, 2025
source_selection.selection_reason: It exposes current FAD, full-range crack growth, residual-stress input, material choices, four notional examples and unresolved cross-software differences.
source_selection.boundary_preserved: The report is guidance, not a substitute for the NASGRO reference manual or API 579. Examples are notional and the local/global Lr discrepancy remains unresolved.

methods: visual inspection of all Griffith pages
section, equation, table and example reconstruction for NASA sources
important_conflicts_retained: Griffith durable energy principle versus his own final numerical correction
NASGRO database toughness 66.8 versus API lower-bound 40.1 in example 13.1
CC27 versus CC28 life difference greater than one order of magnitude in example 13.2
NASGRO versus INSPECT Lr mismatch despite reasonably good SIF/final-crack agreement

content_result.formula_policy: Every display formula has exactly one FormulaNote and every text annotation inside KaTeX is Korean.
content_result.narrative_policy: Observation-to-flaw state precedes energy and K; validity precedes life; FAD precedes inspection; evidence and traceability close the article.

visual_design.grammar: Neutral structural surfaces with sparse blue driving force, teal resistance/evidence, amber boundary and red failure states.
visual_design.interaction_rule: A control must move geometry, a curve, an assessment point, a calculated state or a decision sentence; color-only toggles do not count.
visual_design.responsive_rule: Controls stack on narrow screens, plots keep stable dimensions, all labels stay inside bounds and no visualization creates an inner scrolling surface.
visual_design.shared_fix: FlowRow changes from horizontal at 768px to horizontal at 1024px, preventing six-card plus arrow source reconstructions from creating tablet overflow.
visual_design.animation_boundary: Static causal states were completed first. Decorative motion remains deferred until the prose and all foundation layers are stable.
